title: Host Contract for Extracted Words
statement: Let $S$ and $M$ be finite deterministic machines over the Boolean alphabet, let $V$ be a language of Boolean words, and let $x,v$ be Boolean words and $T,A,d$ natural numbers. Suppose the input-normalized machine derived from $S$ computes $v$ on $x$ in time $T$, and is live at every time $s<T$; suppose also that $M$ decides $V$ within time $A(m+1)^d$ on every input of length $m$. Set $H=2|x|+2+T+(|x|+|v|+2+(A(|x|+|v|+1)^d+1))$. Every Boolean choice word $w$ of length $H$ makes the host built from $S$ and $M$ halt on input $x$ with output the one-bit indicator of $x\mathbin{+�}u\in V$ for some Boolean word $u$ of length $|v|$; conversely, for every such $u$, some choice word $w$ of length $H$ makes that host halt with that output.
hypotheses_covered: Input-normalized $S$ is live at every time $s<T$
$M$ decides $V$ within time $A(m+1)^d$ for every input length $m$
In the converse direction, Boolean word $u$ has length $|v|$
replaced: Let $S$ and $M$ be deterministic machines, $V$ a language, and suppose the input-normalized scheduler on an input $x$ computes a word $v$ within $T$ steps while live earlier, and that $M$ decides $V$ within time $A(m+1)^d$ on inputs of length $m$. Set $H = 2|x| + 2 + T + (|x| + |v| + 2 + (A\,(|x|+|v|+1)^d + 1))$. Then every choice word of length $H$ makes the reverse host built from $S$ and $M$ halt with output the indicator bit of $x\,u \in V$ for some guessed word $u$ of length $|v|$; and conversely, for every $u$ of length $|v|$ some choice word of length $H$ produces a halted run with output the indicator bit of $x\,u \in V$.
